fix_commit.message: Avoid a possible integer overflow when fts5 tokenizes a very large document. Only possible with non-standard builds that use large values of SQLITE_MAX_LENGTH. Bug [bugs:/info/2026-06-09T05:27:16Z | 2026-06-09T05:27:16Z].
fix_commit.author: dan

findings.title: Integer overflow in FTS5 hash entry reallocation size calculation
findings.message: In sqlite3Fts5HashWrite(), when appending to an existing hash entry and more space is needed, the new allocation size is computed as `p->nAlloc * 2`. The field `nAlloc` is declared as `int` (a 32-bit signed integer). If `p->nAlloc` is already large (e.g., >= 0x40000000, possible when SQLITE_MAX_LENGTH is set to a value larger than 2GB), the multiplication overflows before the result is widened to `sqlite3_int64 nNew`. This produces a truncated (potentially negative) 64-bit value, which is then passed to `sqlite3_realloc64()`, causing an incorrect undersized allocation or a failure that should not occur. The fix promotes `p->nAlloc` to `i64` before the multiplication: `(i64)p->nAlloc * 2`.
findings.suggestion: Cast `p->nAlloc` to `i64` (or `sqlite3_int64`) before multiplying by 2 so the arithmetic is performed in 64-bit: `sqlite3_int64 nNew = (i64)p->nAlloc * 2;`

ground_truth.root_cause: The struct field `Fts5HashEntry.nAlloc` is typed as `int` (32-bit signed). The reallocation expression `p->nAlloc * 2` performs 32-bit multiplication; C's implicit integer promotion does not widen to the destination type (`sqlite3_int64`) until after the overflow has already occurred. The fix adds an explicit cast `(i64)` to force 64-bit arithmetic.
